{{nihongo|'''Fuji Sengen Shrine (Togo Town)'''|富士浅間神社}} is a shrine in {{ill|Aichi Prefecture|Q80434|qid=Q80434}}{{ill|Aichi District|Q552687|qid=Q552687|lt=Aichi District}}{{ill|Tōgō, Aichi|Q265050|qid=Q265050}}. There is a theory identifying it with "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ifuno Shrine}}" in Aichi District, Owari Province in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'', though many objections exist. {{nihongo|'''Fuji Sengen Shrine (Togo Town)'''|富士浅間神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

== Overview ==
The founding year is unknown. According to the shrine, the enshrined deities are {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Konohanasakuya-hime-no-Mikoto}}, {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qid=Q272993}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=?mononushi-no-Mikoto}}, and {{ill|Emperor Sujin|Q333530|qid=Q333530}}<ref>[http://sengen3801.jp/concept.html Official site]</ref>.

Since the Edo period, the shrine side has claimed that it is Ifuno Shrine listed in the ''Engishiki Jinmy?ch?''. The theory rests on the fact that the local village name until the Edo period was Y?fukuji, considered similar to "Ifu." However, there are many other candidate shrines for Ifuno Shrine and many competing theories. Based on passages in the surviving text of ''{{ill|Owari no Kuni Fudoki|Q135598023|qid=Q135598023}}'', another theory says Ifuno Shrine was likely in Hibe-go (present-day {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}{{ill|Naka-ku, Nagoya|Q1207921|qid=Q1207921|lt=Naka Ward}}).

== Subsidiary shrines ==
There are Kumano-sha, Izu-sha, Hakusan-sha, Hiyoshi-sha, Kashima-sha, Mishima-sha, Hakone-sha, and others, enshrined in a row behind the main hall. In 1991, a Gokoku Shrine worship hall was also newly established.
